title: The Copper Compass
premise: In 1913, Elodie Reyes drives for a prominent suffragist, secretly reading every letter he carries and memorizing the network of women who trust him with their words. When the seasonal bridge closes and the movement's workshop — holding the printing press and the master list of members — comes under threat from an inheritance dispute that would raze it, Elodie must choose between the invisibility that has kept him safe and the found family who finally see him. As authorities close in and his employer's own letters reveal a betrayal, Elodie races to finish copying and distributing the membership rolls before the workshop falls. He ends by delivering one last letter — his own — choosing love and duty together rather than either alone.
about_author: Sebastian Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffrage-era correspondence in regional collections. The Copper Compass is his second novel, drawn from the marginalia of letters never meant to be read.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. We meet him mid-route, reading letters by lamplight before delivery, measuring his life in what fits in a satchel. He delivers a summons that will trigger the inheritance dispute over the workshop. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; the reader learns he belongs everywhere and nowhere.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Flood season shuts the only road out, stranding him in town with the suffragist circle he serves but has never joined. Mrs. Calloway insists he sleep at the workshop. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy; walls begin to crack as he eats at a table instead of standing beside it.

chapters.title: Letters Never Meant for Him
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with an interlude letter from Thomas Ashford, the estranged heir. Elodie reads correspondence revealing the heir intends to sell the workshop's building within the season. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve; his secret habit becomes his weapon.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating through the women: typesetters, organizers, a teenage apprentice named June who idolizes Elodie. They begin copying the master membership list nightly. Emotional beat: found family crystallizes; Elodie is handed a task no one else can do, and accepts it aloud.

chapters.title: A Man Who Reads
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. June catches him reading a letter meant for Mrs. Calloway. Instead of exposure, she asks him to teach her to read the ciphers the network uses. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into trust; his worst secret becomes a shared craft.

chapters.title: The Heir Arrives
chapters.summary: Thomas Ashford's POV. The heir arrives to inventory the property, expecting vultures, and finds a working household. He and Elodie clash, then recognize each other as men outside their prescribed roles. Emotional beat: antagonism shading into dangerous attraction on both sides.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Employer's Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A letter reveals Mrs. Calloway has been negotiating quietly to sacrifice the workshop to protect the wider movement. Elodie must decide whether to expose her. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal; loyalty fractures along new lines.

chapters.title: Ashes Before Ink
chapters.summary: June's POV. An 'accidental' fire damages the press; the list survives only because Elodie hid it. Suspicion falls on the heir. Emotional beat: fear and fury; the community closes ranks around Elodie, cementing his belonging even as time runs out.

chapters.title: The Last Distribution
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, climax. With the bridge reopening in days and bailiffs behind it, Elodie runs the full route in one night, delivering copied lists to every node in the network while Thomas covers his tracks. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration fused; every skill honed in invisibility spent in open defiance.

chapters.title: His Own Letter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV resolving into shared epilogue voice. The workshop is lost, but the network endures, scattered and untraceable. Elodie writes and delivers a letter under his own name for the first time — to Thomas, and to the family that remains. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined; what cannot be carried was never the point.
